subject: Pilot billing: staggered collection proposal and EU VAT entity handoff
messages:
From: Elena Mirov <elena@medisupply.co>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisupply.co
Date: 2026-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Payment terms and VAT for enterprise pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Medisupply is keen to run the 8-week pilot. Procurement asked me to confirm our desired payment terms and VAT handling so we can issue a PO.

High-level ask: can Redwood accept Net60 for this pilot? Given internal approval cycles and that we'll run the pilot across two EU subsidiaries, we also need the invoices to go to our EU entity (Medisupply GmbH) with VAT on reverse-charge where applicable.

I've attached the draft PO (PO_4532.pdf) for scope and estimated amounts.

Can you confirm what you need from us to route invoices to the EU entity and any impact on credit/collection?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Mirov
Head of Procurement, Medisupply Ltd
elena@medisupply.co
+44 20 5555 1212

Attachments: PO_4532.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mirov <elena@medisupply.co>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Payment terms and VAT for enterprise pilot

Elena — thanks for the PO and for outlining the ask. Good news: we can support invoicing to your EU entity and apply reverse-charge treatment once we have the EU VAT ID and a billing contact. A few things on our side: 

- Credit & collection: Net60 as a standing term will require a short credit intake (+ credit cap), since this is above our standard Net30 for pilots. We typically set a provisional credit corridor for pilots (e.g., initial cap EUR 100,000) and reassess after the first invoice run.
- Alternative to full Net60: we can do a staggered collection schedule to reduce exposure — common pattern we use:
  * 30% upfront at SOW sign
  * 40% at pilot go-live (milestone)
  * Remaining 30% due Net30 after acceptance

If you need the final tranche to be Net45/Net60, we can propose a compromise (increase cap or take a smaller upfront).

Please provide the EU VAT number and the legal invoicing name for Medisupply GmbH. Also confirm who should receive invoices and whether you need us to route invoices to a specific AP email.

I cc'd Marissa from Finance and Karthik from Sales Ops to help with credit and the SOW.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attaches: none

Hi Elena — Marissa from Finance here. Appreciate the clarity. Quick checklist from our side to move forward without delaying the pilot: 

1) Signed SOW referencing PO_4532 (we've prepared a draft SOW reflecting the milestones). I've attached the draft SOW for your review (redwood-sow-draft.pdf).
2) Legal invoicing name and EU VAT ID for Medisupply GmbH.
3) AP email address for invoice delivery and remittance (we can send both PDF invoice and e-invoice).
4) If you require Net60 as a firm term, we will need an increased provisional credit cap. If you can accept the staggered collection schedule Vanessa suggested, we can keep the initial cap lower.

Suggested compromise from finance: accept a milestone schedule with final tranche Net45 instead of Net30, and set a provisional credit cap of EUR 125,000 for the pilot. We'd also add a clause to revisit terms after the pilot finish date.

I've included line items in the SOW for the 30/40/30 milestone schedule. Please review and sign if acceptable.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-sow-draft.pdf (DOCX, draft)

Subject: Re: Payment terms and VAT for enterprise pilot — proposed amendment

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Elena. 

We've reviewed the VAT ID and PO. To bridge Medisupply's internal cadence and Redwood's risk posture, Finance is ok with final tranche Net45 (instead of Net30) under the following conditions: 

1) Provisional credit cap increased to EUR 150,000 for the duration of the pilot (to cover outstanding exposure at Net45).
2) A small prepayment cadence: 10% of subsequent invoices billed in advance on a quarterly basis (this is a standard risk-reduction leaver).
3) We will amend the SOW to reflect Net45 for final tranche and add a clause to re-evaluate credit caps once pilot invoices complete.

Next steps: Vanessa — shall I send the SOW amendment via DocuSign for Elena to sign? I will include updated payment schedule and the provisional cap.

Karthik Iyer
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
